title: Layer caching: instruction order changes build time

videos.script: The same Dockerfile can build in twenty seconds or in a third of one. The difference is the order of its lines. {{key}} Every instruction gets a key: the layer below it, the instruction itself, and the files it copies. If the key matches, the old layer is reused. If it does not, that step runs, and so does every step after it. {{bad}} So copying everything first is expensive. One edited log message, twenty seconds. A new README that the program never reads, twenty seconds again. {{good}} Copy the dependencies first, compile them, and copy the code last. The same edit now takes two seconds, and the README costs nothing. {{mount}} And a cache mount keeps the compiler's own cache between builds, without putting it in the image.
